engage at both strategic and operational level. 

contribute to the department's formal reviews of the local area/local area partnership's progress and make a recommendation to VCU on whether progress has been sufficient. 

provide regular written reports to the department on the local area/local area partnership's progress to VCU, and more frequently if the pace of progress is not sufficient.  

have an awareness of the proposed SEND/AP system and Children's Social Care reforms including the Change Programme and work closely with relevant colleagues in supporting and challenging local areas/local area partnerships. 

develop working relationships with Health partners where this helps achieve the objectives set out in the contract.

title: For the Provision of an  Emotional Health and Wellbeing Service for Children in Care
description:
Derby City Council (the Council) is undertaking this procurement on behalf of itself and the Derby and Derbyshire NHS Integrated Commissioning Board to establish a contract for the provision of an Emotional Health and Wellbeing Service for Children in Care. 

We seek a single provider, lead provider, or consortium to deliver a trauma informed service which embeds and delivers interventions to children in care (CIC) and their therapeutic parenting team which meets their individual emotional and mental health needs and creates stability in placements.  

The service will ensure the needs of the child are paramount, using a range of interventions via direct or indirect work. This will deliver to all children in care who meet the inclusion criteria, including those children who are placed within the Local Authority boundaries from other areas. It will also include those who are cared for by the Local Authorities approved foster carers, that live never more than 5 miles outside of the Derbyshire Footprint.

The overall aim of the service is to improve the emotional health and wellbeing of CIC via direct support to the child and / or indirect support to the therapeutic parenting team.

The service will offer a range of appropriate evidence based, trauma informed interventions, both group and one to one.  The service is not expected to prescribe medications, nor does it need to be CQC registered.

In addition to the core specification, we are including a two year "proof of concept" service for Children in Care with complex needs through a Coordination and Advisory Team. The contract period for this element is 19 months; commencing in line with the core requirement on 1st September 2025 and expiring 31st March 2027. (the incumbent provider is expecting to commence the service within its existing service delivery from April 2025).

For information: The agreement with the successful bidder will have, as parties to it, Derby City Council, NHS Derby and Derbyshire Integrated Care Board and Derbyshire County Council. Derby City Council and Derbyshire County Council will refer young people to the service and both, with the additional of the NHS Derby and Derbyshire Integrated Care Board, will be responsible for the contract management.

title: CPH074  Suicide Prevention and Mental Health Related Training and Stakeholder Event
description:
Derbyshire County Council are seeking to procure under the Restricted Process, a sole provider or consortium (working as one entity), with relevant experience and expertise, to deliver a programme of two courses, Suicide Awareness and Managing Mental Health Conversations and Mental Health Awareness training. 

The process will include a request to participate, pre-qualification stage, following the assessment at the request to participate stage, the Council will limit the number of bidders invited to participate in the Invitation to Tender to the top 5 highest scoring tenders based on the assessment of the pre-qualification. 

The course are Suicide Awareness and Managing Mental Health Conversations training and Mental Health Awareness training, each tailored to this Specification to be delivered across Derbyshire only (excluding Derby City). The training will be aimed at target organisations, which include a broad range of statutory, community and voluntary sector organisations and places will be free to participants. Training will comprise a mix of both face-to-face training sessions and virtual online (live trainer delivered) interactive training sessions. Such training is supported by national recommendations and is reflective of good practice. 

Alongside the training, the Provider will be required to organise and deliver the annual stakeholder event of the Derbyshire Self-Harm and Suicide Prevention Partnership Forum (DSSPPF) in each of the years of the contract. The DSSPPF includes both Derbyshire County and Derby City organisations and is the local suicide prevention partnership. 

The mobilisation period will be from 30 January 2023 to service contract start date.

The initial contract period is for 1 year commencing on the 01 March 2023 with the option to extend for a further 2 periods of 24 months (a maximum total of five years).

title: Regional SEND Mediation Advice, Mediation and Disagreement Resolution Services
description:
On behalf of all Local Authorities in the East Midlands, Lincolnshire County Council is leading the procurement of Regional SEND Mediation Advice Services, Mediation Services and Disagreement Resolution (DR) Services.\r
\r
The East Midlands Region is made up of ten (10) Local Authorities (LAs) as listed below:\r
Derby City Council\r
Derbyshire County Council\r
Leicester City Council\r
Leicestershire County Council\r
Lincolnshire County Council\r
North Northamptonshire Council\r
West Northamptonshire Council\r
Nottingham City Council\r
Nottinghamshire County Council\r
Rutland County Council\r
\r
The Service shall consist of three (3) elements: Mediation Advice Services, Mediation Services and DR Services, and shall be delivered to CYP with SEND aged 0-25 years living within the East Midlands. \r
\r
Lincolnshire County Council will act as the Lead Authority on behalf of all ten (10) LAs within East Midlands for the procurement and contract management of the service: however, the successful Supplier will enter into individual agreements with each LA to deliver the Service.\r
\r
All ten LAs (the Customer) require the supply of unbiased Mediation Advice Services, Mediation Services and DR Services (The Service) for Children and Young People (CYP) with Special Educational Needs and/or Disabilities (SEND) and their families as part of the single route of redress from 1st November 2023. For the avoidance of doubt this means that the Service shall be fully operational from the 1st November 2023.\r
\r
The Children and Families Act (2014) sets out the way in which services and provision are made for families of CYP with SEND aged 0-25 years. This Act, specifically Sections 51-57 and 60, defines the statutory duties for local authorities with regard to appeals, Mediation Advice, Mediation and DR Services, along with Chapter 11 of the associated SEND Code of Practise (COP) 2015. This service shall have due regard to relevant legislation and ensure it supports LAs to meet their statutory duty and the needs of CYP with SEND. \r
\r
Mediation Advice Services and Mediation Services are in place to help settle disputes between CYP, families and LAs relating to Education, Health, and Care (EHC) Needs Assessment requests, EHC Needs Assessments or elements of content within the EHC Plan (EHCP). \r
\r
DR is voluntary for all parties and complements Mediation Advice and Mediation to resolve disagreements which may be related to the fulfilment of duties, SEND provision and health and social care provision for CYP with SEND, including disagreements between health commissioners and LAs.\r
\r
An online supplier briefing event will be held on Monday 26th June 2023 at 10:00am. The online event will briefly outline the requirements of the delivery of Mediation Advice Services, Mediation Services and DR Services in the East Midlands. To book into the briefing event please email fliss.christopher@lincolnshire.gov.uk.

title: Flexible Open Framework for the Provision of Supported Living Services
description:
Derby City Council seeks to create a Flexible Open Framework for the provision of Supported Living Services under the Light Touch Regime of the Contract Regulations 2015, for adults and young people aged 16+ with eligible assessed needs within their own accommodation. This Framework will replace the current Derby City Support and Accommodation Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS). 

Partner organisations such as Derbyshire County Council, Nottingham City Council and Nottinghamshire County Council (referred to as D2N2), Integrated Care Board (ICB) and NHS organisations within the D2N2 area and Derby Homes may access the Framework and use the 'Call Off' arrangements, under their own individual terms and conditions. 

Bidders may apply for one or more of the following Lots: 
•	Lot 1- Low Needs
•	Lot 2 - Medium Needs 
•	Lot 3 - High Needs

There will be no minimum or maximum number of Service Providers that may be successful in each Lot, and no limit on the number of Lots Bidders can be successful in.

Bidders must have the appropriate registration with the health and social care regulator for England, the Care Quality Commission (CQC) for the delivery of the regulated activity of personal care to apply. 

Service Providers will be required to demonstrate competence to deliver the Service to Customers on an individual basis based on their social care assessed needs and preferences, including demonstration of skills and experience required.

Bidders, submitting responses that include Service Models for accommodation (Settings) under any LOT, will be required to registered with Decent and Safe Homes (DASH) Derby City Council Accreditation Scheme (DASH) and subsequently accredited, prior to delivering any Support within this Framework. The service will need to;
• Provide appropriate orthotics, inclusive of elastic/fabric and custom-made splints. To provide advice to maximise children's' motor skills, minimise development of contracture and deformity in the growing child and prevent injury in a caseload of children with neurological and physical health needs.

• Facilitate the treatment and rehabilitation of the patient. This is achieved through the assessment of need and the provision of an orthoses that will either remedy or relieve a medical condition or disability and may prevent the development of more disabling conditions.

• Provide access to high quality, safe care that gives timely advice, appropriate support, assessment, diagnosis, and treatment for patients according to their individual need.

• Ensure the service is delivered in line with current policy, learning and best evidence and provide appropriate governance and management for the service.

The contract will commence 01st June 2025 and be 3 years with the Commissioner having the option to extend the Contract for up to a further 2 years.

title: Request for Quotation - Derby Safe Haven
description:
NHS Derby & Derbyshire Integrated Care Board (formerly Clinical Commissioning Group) sought to commission a Derby Safe Haven service to be delivered across the population of Derby and Derbyshire. 

The overall aim of the Derby Safe Haven is to establish a safe, non-clinical environment whereby people with urgent mental health needs - who would otherwise require or seek support from Accident and Emergency secondary or acute mental health services - can receive support and de-escalation.

The service was to be situated in Derby in a fixed and accessible location that maximises access across not only within Derby City, but for people across the rest of the Derbyshire footprint also.

The service contract is for 2 years with the option to extend for a further 12 months. It is recognised that the service and the system will need to learn and adapt to the dynamic needs of the population throughout the duration of the service, and collaborative working between provider and commissioners will be critical to success. 

Please note there was a financial threshold associated with this procurement. Any bids received exceeding £200,000 per annum over the term of the contract were to be excluded from evaluation and disqualified from the process. No bids over £200,000 per annum were to be accepted.

title: Local Plan Development Options, Traffic and Transportation Assessment and Flood Risk Assessment (L2 SFRA)
description:
A contract has been awarded following a call off by re-opening competition under the Homes England, Development and Regeneration Technical Services (DARTS) Framework 2023-2027, Lot 1 - end-to-end technical and professional services.

The overall objective of the commission is consultancy services to provide advice to the Council on whether in practical terms there is any realistic prospects that the level of residential development identified as being necessary to meet its future growth aspirations can be delivered, and in a way which will achieve the objectives of delivering sustainable development. 

The requirements are 

Provide advice to support the delivery of the Government's revised housing targets through the identification of sustainable options for the development of communities within the Derbyshire Dales local planning authority area for the period up to 2045

Provide evidence relating to traffic and transportation to support the emerging Derbyshire Dales Local Plan

Undertake a Level 2 Strategic Flood Risk Assessment to assess the cumulative effects of potential development sites within the defined High Sensitive Catchment to assess how the cumulative effects of development sites could impact peak flows, the duration of flooding and timing of flood peaks on receiving watercourses. 

The initial contract period is 12 months.  There will be an option to extend the contract for 12 months, subject to satisfactory performance and business needs. Maximum contract period is two years.
